previous_statement: Applying nodes 1.4 and 1.5 to the two terms on the right gives ||m*(q - beta)||_1 <= sum_j b_j*dist_1(p_j, C) + sum_k c_k*D_k, and combining with the preceding distance estimate proves the root claim.
new_statement: The final inequality follows by a local chain: beta in C and m>0 give m*dist_1(q,C) <= ||m*(q-beta)||_1; the identity m*(q-beta)=sum_j b_j*(p_j-beta_j)+sum_k c_k*(beta-r_k) and the l1 triangle inequality bound this by the sum of the positive and negative residual norms; those residual norms are bounded respectively by sum_j b_j*dist_1(p_j,C) and sum_k c_k*D_k. Therefore m*dist_1(q,C) <= sum_j b_j*dist_1(p_j,C) + sum_k c_k*D_k.
